rows.title: Ship traffic through the Suez Canal week of November 23?
rows.original: Ship traffic through the Suez Canal week of November 23?

markets.question: Will 280+ ships transit the Suez Canal week of November 23?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the total number of transit calls through the Suez Canal from November 23, 2026 to November 29, 2026, according to IMF PortWatch, is at least the number specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The total is the sum of the daily figures for every date in the period. Daily figures are the total transit calls by container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships that IMF PortWatch publishes for each date.

This market will resolve once IMF PortWatch has published data for every date in the period. Revisions made after that point will not be considered, unless subject to the data integrity clause below. If any data is still unpublished 14 calendar days after the period’s final date, this market will resolve on the most recent data published at that time.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the Transit Calls data published for the Suez Canal at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/c57c79bf612b4372b08a9c6ea9c97ef0.

rows.title: How low will 30-year Treasury yield get before 2027?
rows.original: How low will 30-year Treasury yield get before 2027?

markets.question: Will the 30-year Treasury yield dip below 4.60% before 2027?
markets.label: Below 4.60%
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 30-year yield is lower than the listed value for any date between September 2, 2026 and December 31, 2026. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve as soon as the Treasury 30-year yield is lower than the listed value, or once data is available for December 31, 2026. If no qualifying value is published and data is not available for December 31, 2026 by January 14, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "30 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026).

markets.question: Will the median home value in the Chicago Metro be less than $303,000 on December 31?
markets.label: <$303K
markets.rules:
This market will resolve according to the median home value for all property types in Chicago Metro, IL on December 31, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The resolution source will be official data from the Parcl Labs Sales Price Index for Chicago Metro, IL (Parcl_ID: 2899845). rows.title: Core PCE MoM - November 2026
rows.original: Core PCE MoM - November 2026

markets.question: Will Core PCE MoM be 0.0% or less in November?
markets.rules:
This is a market about core inflation (excluding food and energy) over the 1-month period ending November 2026, seasonally adjusted, as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

This market will resolve to the percentage change in the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index excluding food and energy (Core PCE) over the 1-month period ending in November 2026 according to the monthly Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) report.

The resolution source for this market will be the BEA Personal Income and Outlays report for November 2026 (https://www.bea.gov/data/personal-consumption-expenditures-price-index), currently scheduled to be released on December 23, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET. Resolution of this market will take place upon release of the aforementioned data.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the official monthly BEA Personal Income and Outlays news release, which reports core inflation (all items less food and energy) over 1-month periods to only one decimal point (e.g., 0.2%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market. For the avoidance of doubt, this market resolves on the core PCE figure — the PCE price index excluding food and energy — not the headline all-items (total) PCE price index figure.

If the BEA does not release the relevant figures on the scheduled date, this market may remain open up until the scheduled release time of the next Personal Income and Outlays report (https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule). If the information is not released by that time, this market will resolve according to the figures of the most recent previous month with available data.

rows.title: November Inflation China - Monthly
rows.original: November Inflation China - Monthly

markets.question: Will China's monthly inflation increase by ≤0.0% in November?
markets.rules:
This is a market about the monthly variation of consumer prices in China as reported by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) of China.

This market will resolve according to the number the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by in November 2026 (% change from the previous month) according to the monthly NBS report.

The resolution source for this market will be the NBS Consumer Price Index monthly report released for November 2026 (https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/), currently scheduled to be released in December 2026. Resolution of this market will take place upon release of the aforementioned data. If no data for the specified month is released by the date the next month's data is scheduled to be released, this market will resolve based on data from the last available month.

You can find the relevant figure by locating the report for November 2026 on the Press Releases page (see: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/), locating the table named "Consumer Price Index in November 2026", and finding the consumer price index figure in the column labeled "Growth Rate M/M (%)".

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the official monthly NBS CPI news release which reports monthly inflation to only one decimal point (e.g. 1.9%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market. For the full release schedule, see: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/ReleaseCalendar/

rows.title: Highest 7-day average ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by January 31?
rows.original: Highest 7-day average ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by January 31?

markets.question: Will the 7-day average ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz reach 4+ by January 31?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the 7-day moving average of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz for any single date between market creation and January 31, 2027, according to IMF PortWatch, is at least the number specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

IMF PortWatch typically publishes a rounded 7-day moving average in the chart on its chokepoint page and an unrounded figure in its downloadable files. The figure shown in the chart will be used for settlement. If the chart is unavailable, the downloadable figure, rounded to the nearest whole number, will be used.

This market will resolve once IMF PortWatch has published data for every date in the period. Revisions made after that point will not be considered, unless subject to the data integrity clause below. If any data is still unpublished 14 calendar days after the period’s final date, this market will resolve on the most recent data published at that time.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the Transit Calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730.

rows.title: Japan GDP growth in Q4 2026 (QoQ Annualized)?
rows.original: Japan GDP growth in Q4 2026 (QoQ Annualized)?

markets.question: Will Japan Q4 GDP growth (annualized) be less than -3.2%?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve according to Japan's real gross domestic product growth rate (Quarter-over-Quarter Annualized, %, seasonally adjusted) in the fourth quarter of 2026, as reported in the Japan Cabinet Office's (ESRI) Quarterly Estimates of GDP (First Preliminary Estimates) release for Oct.-Dec. 2026, scheduled for release on February 15, 2027.

The relevant figure is the "GDP (Expenditure Approach)" value for the "2026/10-12." row in the table titled "Real, Seasonally Adjusted Series (Quarter-to-Quarter, Annualized)", found under the heading "I. GDP (Expenditure Approach) and Its Components" on the release page for Oct.-Dec. 2026 (The 1st preliminary). This figure expresses the quarterly growth rate compounded over four quarters to produce an annualized equivalent; the non-annualized "Quarter-to-Quarter" figure will not be used.

To find the release page: go to https://www.esri.cao.go.jp/en/sna/sokuhou/sokuhou_top.html and click "Time series table" (which links to the latest release), or go to the Release Archive (https://www.esri.cao.go.jp/en/sna/data/sokuhou/files/toukei_top.html), select 2027, and click "Quarterly Estimates of GDP for Oct.-Dec.2026 (The First preliminary Estimates)". The same figure published in the release's summary PDF ("1-1. GDP (Expenditure Approach) and Its Components") may also be used. Changes in the Japan Cabinet Office's GDP reporting format will not disqualify a published figure from counting.

rows.original: US GDP growth in Q4 2026?

markets.question: Will US GDP growth in Q4 2026 be less than 1.5%?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2026, scheduled for January 28, 2027.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

If the advance estimate is not released, this market will resolve based on the first officially published figure for real GDP for the specified quarter (e.g., the ‘second’ or ‘third’ estimate, etc.), as reported by the BEA. If no official estimate is released by the date the next quarter's advanced estimate is scheduled to be published, this market will resolve based on the most recent previous figure released by the BEA.

rows.title: Reserve Bank of Australia Decision in February?
rows.original: Reserve Bank of Australia Decision in February?

markets.question: Will the Reserve Bank of Australia decrease the cash rate target by 50+ bps at the February meeting?
markets.label: 降息50基点及以上
markets.rules:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the cash rate target resulting from the February 2027 meeting of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Monetary Policy Board, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting. 

The resolution source will be official information from the Reserve Bank of Australia, including the statement or release from its February 2027 meeting, scheduled for February 8 and February 9, 2027, as listed on the official RBA calendar (https://www.rba.gov.au/schedules-events/calendar/?topics=monetary-policy-board). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board resulting from its February 2027 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

rows.title: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?
rows.original: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?

markets.question: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?
markets.label: Yes（是）
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds an emergency meeting after which the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lowered between November 11, 2025 and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An emergency meeting is defined as any unscheduled meeting called by the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) apart from the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2025 and the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2026.

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Federal Reserve’s website (federalreserve.gov) or credible news sources reporting on the emergency meeting.

rows.title: 7-day average ship traffic through the Panama Canal on January 31?
rows.original: 7-day average ship traffic through the Panama Canal on January 31?

markets.question: Will the 7-day average ship traffic through the Panama Canal be 24+ on January 31?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the 7-day moving average of transit calls through the Panama Canal for January 31, 2027, according to IMF PortWatch, is at least the number specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

IMF PortWatch typically publishes a rounded 7-day moving average in the chart on its chokepoint page and an unrounded figure in its downloadable files. The figure shown in the chart will be used for settlement. If the chart is unavailable, the downloadable figure, rounded to the nearest whole number, will be used.

This market will resolve once IMF PortWatch has published data for January 31, 2027. Revisions made after that point will not be considered, unless subject to the data integrity clause below. If that data is still unpublished 14 calendar days after January 31, 2027, this market will resolve on the most recent data published at that time.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the Transit Calls data published for the Panama Canal at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/44d73fd00bbc4f73a16d46d5beb11b4d.

rows.title: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz week of November 23?
rows.original: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz week of November 23?

markets.question: Will 22+ ships transit the Strait of Hormuz week of November 23?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the total number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz from November 23, 2026 to November 29, 2026, according to IMF PortWatch, is at least the number specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The total is the sum of the daily figures for every date in the period. Daily figures are the total transit calls by container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships that IMF PortWatch publishes for each date.

This market will resolve once IMF PortWatch has published data for every date in the period. Revisions made after that point will not be considered, unless subject to the data integrity clause below. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

markets.question: CoreWeave downgraded by Moody's or S&P by December 31, 2026?
markets.label: December 31, 2026
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if either Moody's Ratings or S&P Global Ratings publishes a rating action lowering its long-term credit rating for CoreWeave, Inc., or its rating on CoreWeave, Inc.'s senior unsecured debt, by 11:59 PM ET on the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

"Long-term credit rating" means S&P Global Ratings' long-term issuer credit rating, or Moody's Ratings' corporate family rating or long-term issuer rating, on CoreWeave, Inc.

A downgrade of CoreWeave, Inc.'s senior unsecured debt by either agency will qualify, even if that agency's long-term credit rating for CoreWeave, Inc. is unchanged.

A change in outlook or CreditWatch/review status alone (for example, a move from Stable to Negative outlook, or placement on review for downgrade) will not qualify.

As of market creation, CoreWeave, Inc. is rated B+ by S&P Global Ratings (https://cbonds.com/news/3865295/) and Ba3 by Moody's Ratings (https://cbonds.com/news/3865521/), both below investment grade.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be the official rating action publications of Moody's Ratings (https://ratings.moodys.com) and S&P Global Ratings (https://www.spglobal.com/ratings); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

rows.title: Highest 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait by January 31?
rows.original: Highest 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait by January 31?

markets.question: Will the 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait reach 28+ by January 31?
markets.rules:

rows.title: 2026 World GDP Growth
rows.original: 2026 World GDP Growth

markets.question: Will world GDP growth be ≤2.9% in 2026?
markets.rules:
This Market will resolve according to the estimate of the World GDP growth rate (Real GDP, annual percent change) reported by the International Monetary Fund in the World Economic Outlook Update released between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, expected to be released in January 2027. 

The relevant figure may be found in the table titled “World Economic Outlook Growth Projections” under “Estimate” in the row “World Output” and the column “2026”. Changes in the IMF’s World Economic Outlook reporting format will not disqualify a published figure from counting.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/weo

If no estimate of the 2026 annual percent change in world real GDP is released in a World Economic Outlook Update between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, this market will resolve according to the published figure for 2026 annual percent change in World real GDP in the April 2027 edition of the World Economic Outlook. If no such figure is published by April 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

If multiple World Economic Outlook Updates are released between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, this market will resolve based on the first such publication which includes an estimate of the 2026 annual percent change in World GDP. Projections of World GDP, however, will not be considered.

Note: data from the initial release of the referenced GDP report is what will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following release or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the initial release will not be considered for this market's resolution.

Note: the resolution source for this market reports annual percent change in world real GDP to one decimal point (e.g. 3.3%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

rows.title: ECB Interest Rates: December 2026
rows.original: ECB Interest Rates: December 2026

markets.question: Will the ECB announce a 50+ bps decrease at the December 2026 meeting?
markets.label: 降息50基点及以上
markets.rules:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the deposit facility rate resulting from the December 2026 meeting of the European Central Bank, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the European Central Bank, including the statement or release from its December 2026 meeting, scheduled for December 16-17, 2026, as listed on the official European Central Bank calendar (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the European Central Bank's December 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

rows.original: How high will US unemployment go in 2026?

markets.question: Will US unemployment reach at least 5.0% in 2026?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (total unemployed, as a percent of the civilian labor force, official unemployment rate denoted as U-3) reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in an “Employment Situation Report” for a reference month in 2026 is greater than or equal to the listed percentage. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The relevant reports for this market are the Employment Situation Reports for January-December, 2026. This market may not resolve to “No” until the Employment Situation report for December 2026 is released. If no Employment Situation Report for December 2026 is released by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, however, this market will resolve based on all previously published data up to that time. 

The resolution source for this market is the Monthly Employment Situation Report, published by the BLS every month at https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm, specifically the U-3 measure in Table A-15 for each month.

Note: the resolution source for this market reports unemployment to one decimal point. Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

rows.title: 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on December 31?
rows.original: 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on December 31?

markets.question: Will the 7-day average ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait be 22+ on December 31?
markets.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the 7-day moving average of transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait for December 31, 2026, according to IMF PortWatch, is at least the number specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

IMF PortWatch typically publishes a rounded 7-day moving average in the chart on its chokepoint page and an unrounded figure in its downloadable files. The figure shown in the chart will be used for settlement. If the chart is unavailable, the downloadable figure, rounded to the nearest whole number, will be used.

This market will resolve once IMF PortWatch has published data for December 31, 2026. Revisions made after that point will not be considered, unless subject to the data integrity clause below. If that data is still unpublished 14 calendar days after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve on the most recent data published at that time.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the Transit Calls data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.
